$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{3-4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot (-\frac{1}{4})\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-4x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the above by writing $C=-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡K$ for another arbitrary constant $K,$ and then we can combine the two terms using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-4x|+C & =-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-4x|-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|3-4x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡K) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|3-4x|)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we finally conclude that

$$
\int \frac{1}{3-4x}\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|3-4x|).
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["cce4b3ec-222e-51ba-8ae8-114a9fa9d3d6"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "0ed309e1-7fed-5611-88ea-d3f7f560e643" "Calculate $\int \frac{1}{6x+2}\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant." :question/worked-solution "First, let $u=6x+2.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{6}\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{6x+2}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡|6x+2|+C\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the above by writing $C=\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡K$ for another arbitrary constant $K,$ and then we can combine the two terms using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡|6x+2|+C & =\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡|6x+2|+\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|6x+2|+\operatorname{ln}⁡K) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|6x+2|)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we finally conclude that

$$
\int \frac{1}{6x+2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|6x+2|).
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["85668fa6-214c-50d9-8486-30cba7ace9ed"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "13d0d069-d025-565b-a9ec-455ab0bce8a9"
